# Secondary control-function reference

`secondary_functions_reference.json` is generated by
`../scripts/generate_secondary_functions_reference.py`. It executes the complete
fixed upstream `SecondaryAxis` class through the accepted D40 numeric source
loader. MoonBit tests consume original-source values, never values calculated by
the port to construct an expectation.

The new package has 40 parameter/lifecycle records: 26 typed pair/reset projections
and 14 explicitly source-only dynamic parameter records. It also retains the six
nonlinear stages first collected independently during render preparation. Those
46 observations produce 27 private Scene scenario functions in one registered
test group: 26 parameter scenarios plus one sequential six-stage scenario. These
counts are separate from D40's 53 observations and do not represent 46 independent
renderer parity tests.

The generated files are:

- `secondary_functions_reference.json`: native states, exceptions, identities,
  events and nonlinear transform/display observations.
- `../scene/secondary_functions_reference_wbtest.mbt`: grouped typed projections.

The generator and these two outputs are reproducible with:

```sh
/Users/lampese/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python3 \
  scripts/generate_secondary_functions_reference.py \
  .moonagent/upstream/matplotlib-v3.11.2/lib/matplotlib/ticker.py
/Users/lampese/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python3 \
  scripts/generate_secondary_functions_reference.py \
  .moonagent/upstream/matplotlib-v3.11.2/lib/matplotlib/ticker.py --check
```

## Source host and typed bridge

The stable loader is
`generate_secondary_lifecycle_reference.load_secondary_source(path)`. Complete
original Secondary construction, setters, `_set_scale`, `_set_lims`, aspect and
draw bodies execute. Original function transforms/scales, Axis scale/default
installation, limits and autoscale, real Bboxes and `child.transData` also execute.
Graphical superclass construction is the D40 numerical storage/style host, and
super.draw is its presentation sink. This is not full GUI, tick-artist or glyph
renderer execution. The new generator does not replace a source setter, locator,
transform or autoscale algorithm.

The typed API accepts two nonraising `Double -> Double` callbacks through
`set_functions(forward, inverse)`. `reset_functions()` represents the native None
branch by storing identity callbacks. Existing two-callback constructors remain;
constructor None is projected to an identity pair without adding another public
constructor surface. The public `forward()` and `inverse()` getters return their
current callable values. Retained old getter results remain old callable values.

Native tuple object identity, Transform subclasses, vector shape/aliasing and
invalid dynamic parameter inputs are retained as source-only metadata. In
particular a list of two callables is invalid, tuple length must be two, both
components must be callable, and a Transform is accepted without eager dimension
or invertibility checking. The base Transform can construct successfully and fail
only when its transform/inversion is consumed. These inputs cannot be passed to
the statically typed two-function setter; no invented validation is added there.

## Observable lifecycle

The source setter validates its input, assigns the new pair, then calls
`_set_scale`. It does not first synchronize parent limits or clear the cached
parent name. Equal parent names retain all four ticker objects, default flags,
installed transform and stored own view. New controls are visible immediately.
A later aspect/draw maps parent limits through the new forward callback while
still using the previously installed transform until a genuine name change.

The nonlinear sequence starts from parent `[1,4]` and old controls `2*x, x/2`.
Changing controls to `x*x, sqrt(x)` leaves the installed inverse `x/2` in place.
Aspect updates own view to `[1,16]`; same-name draw keeps that old transform.
A change from linear to symlog installs the new inverse despite both child scales
being called `function`. None reset then maps identity limits `[1,4]` while the
installed inverse remains `sqrt(x)` until another parent-name change.

The source JSON preserves the original actual-transData positions for those six
stages. Generated Scene tests assert exact own views, sampled installed mapping
and additional original transform endpoint measurements. They do not reproduce
the renderer normalization formula. Separate focused render tests exercise the
render projection. Native transform identity is recorded, while typed tests
verify its observable numerical mapping rather than physical closure identity.

On a real name change, the setter immediately uses the D40 lifecycle: read CURRENT
major tick locations if latched, install function/functionlog and defaults, run
conditional own-empty-data autoscale, restore current ticks as a fresh Fixed
locator, and only then commit the parent-name cache. It does not substitute the
old `set_ticks` input for current locator output.

The Int64 slice scenario calls `set_ticks([2,3])`, then replaces the major locator
with the borrowed view `[4,7]` from Int64 owner `[1,4,7,9]`. Reinstallation keeps the
CURRENT view and its dtype. Writing the new Fixed result changes both the owner
and the old locator's view; their old owner binding remains usable. The original
source's identical-view relation is directly checked in the typed projection.

## Failures and successful NaN fallback

Four x/y × pair/reset records prove a checked failure after pair assignment.
With the latch set and CURRENT LogLocator bound to own `[0,1]` with minpos Inf,
parent name change makes the current-tick query fail before defaults/context
installation. New controls survive, but old slots, own view, installed transform,
cache and persistent latch remain. Native ValueError type/message remain verbatim
in JSON. The Moon test checks the existing `Core.DataError::InvalidTicks` mapping
and exact surviving state. Existing typed error text is not presented as verbatim
native exception-message parity.

NaN forward is deliberately not rejected at setter receipt. With an unchanged
parent name, it stores successfully; later aspect fails finite limit validation
without changing the old view/context. A different case changes the parent name
to log before storing NaN forward: actual source LogLocator.view_limits normalizes
the NaN autoscale candidates to `[1,10]`, so this setter succeeds with fresh defaults
and cache `log`. The successful fallback is retained as an explicit regression.
No imaginary post-install failure or additional callback effect API is introduced.

All finite expected doubles are encoded from original binary64 bits and compared
exactly. NaN output classification is checked without a NaN payload claim. There
is no tolerance, finite-value substitution, resource cap or ignored native error.
Arbitrary Python callback exceptions and general vector return shapes remain
source-only; the existing typed callback effect domain is unchanged.

## Generation and verification status

The first formal generation preserved all 40 complete preparation records exactly.
All original fields in the independent six nonlinear records also remained equal;
only extra original installed-transform endpoint measurements were added to those
six records. Old D40 generators and JSON files were untouched.

The generator's `--check` verifies source regeneration and both generated outputs.
It uses the existing stdin-only formatter for the one emitted MoonBit file.
Project check/test/info/full-format/interface and acceptance remain Root's unified
workflow after all writers stop. Source `--check` success alone is not a claim that
MoonBit behavior has passed that acceptance gate.

D41 acceptance passed the complete four-target suite: wasm/wasm-gc/native each
22001/22001 and JS 22008/22008, with zero failures. This slice adds 11 registered
tests: the one generated group containing 27 scenarios, six lifecycle hands and
four retained-IR/render hands. All 40 original preparation records and every old
field in the six nonlinear records remain unchanged. The reviewed 21-line public
interface diff adds the two setters and replaces two readonly fields with private
mutable storage while retaining both callable getters. The only compile repairs
were typed FixedLocator.values query spelling and a StringView allocation helper;
source values, tolerances and production lifecycle rules were not altered.
